Systems codex

The live numbers powering the vertical slice. Everything on this page is imported from the same content tables the game engine reads at runtime — the doc cannot drift from the build.

Progression curve

xp(n) = 60 · n^1.85 — deliberately steep from level 8, so the 10% death penalty in the Barrow costs a real evening rather than a real month.

Auto-attack tick

every 2000ms · dmg = 6 + floor(lv · 0.9) + weapon

Melee reach only. Any manual ability resets the tick, so active play is always faster.

Damage & mitigation

dmg = max(1, (base + floor(lv · 1.6) + weapon) − armour)

Flat mitigation, never percentages. Crit is a flat 14% for ×1.85 so the maths stays head-doable.

Encumbrance

step = 205 + min(90, heavy · 5) ms

The counterweight to armour. Full plate costs 40ms per tile, which is a real telegraph tax.

Death penalty

xp -= xp · 0.10 · gold -= carried · 0.50

Applied instantly. A Remnant cache spawns on the exact tile and is written to the world feed.

Regeneration

+1 + floor(lv/3) hp · +2 + floor(lv/2) mp per 1.4s

Slow on purpose. Downtime is where the market for salves and draughts comes from.

Full Barrow plate

🛡 27Husk → 1 dmg295ms

Everything equipped. Nothing in the game hits you for more than 1 — but you step at 295ms.

Loot rules

3×3

1 sqm spread

Drops distribute across the walkable tiles around the corpse, corpse tile first. Nine items never stack into one unreadable 44px pile.

60s

Claim window

The top damage dealer holds exclusive rights. A lock icon plus a depleting red arc renders on every protected stack.

3min

Ground decay

After that the stack is deleted. Unclaimed wealth leaves the economy — a passive gold sink.

hide

Filter

Excluded items are not rendered, not tappable, and skipped by auto pick-up. Purely a clarity tool, never a drop-rate modifier.

Touch controls

  • Left stick — 8-way grid stepping, 205ms + encumbrance
  • Tap a creature — Mark it; starts the 2s auto-attack tick
  • Drag a creature → release — shove it 1 tile, cancelling its wind-up
  • Tap a loot stack — take it if adjacent and unlocked
  • Mark pad — cycle nearest hostiles within 6 tiles
  • Loot pad — sweep all claimable filtered loot within 1 tile
  • 4 action pads — Strike / Cleave / Ash Bolt / Ward
  • Walk onto a stack — auto pick-up, if enabled

Desktop parity

  • WASD / arrows — movement
  • 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 — abilities (Space = Strike)
  • Tab — cycle Mark
  • Click — Mark / loot, identical to tap
  • Hold left-click on a creature, drag, release — shove. Same gesture, same code path as touch.
  • G — loot everything nearby
  • I · C · F — satchel · character · loot filter

Desktop never receives extra information or extra actions. Any advantage there would fracture a shared persistent world.
